exam_structure.paper_name: Greece and Persia — Greek Depth Study
exam_structure.overview: Q16(a)–(c) Discrete factual knowledge (5m, AO1); Q17 What can we learn from Prescribed Source/Passage (5m, AO3); Q18 How accurate is the Prescribed Source/Passage presentation (5m, AO3); Q19 Second-order concept explanation (10m: 5 AO1 + 5 AO2 — zero source reliability needed); Q20* Evaluative essay analysing Prescribed Ancient Sources + own knowledge (20m: 5 AO1 + 5 AO2 + 10 AO3).

archaeological: Mosaic from the House of the Faun in Pompeii depicting Darius and Alexander
The Alexander sarcophagus, showing Alexander at the Battle of Issus
Babylonian Astronomical Diary tablet mentioning the Battle of Gaugamela (British Museum)
Silver tetradrachm minted by Lysimachus showing Alexander with horns, Zeus Ammon and Athena (BM: 1919, 0820.1)
Silver tetradrachm minted by Ptolemy I showing Alexander with elephant scalp headdress (BM: 1987, 0649.508)

sections.title: Key Topic 1: Youth, Accession, Character & Beliefs (356–334 BC)

topics.title: 1.1 Youth, Olympias, Philip and Divine Lineage
points: Alexander's youth; the character, political and personal influence of Olympias; Alexander's relationship with Philip
prescribedSetSources: Silver tetradrachm minted by Lysimachus showing Alexander with horns, Zeus Ammon and Athena

topics.title: 1.2 Murder of Philip and Expedition Against Persia
points: The murder of Philip and the differing interpretations of the events surrounding it
The initial reasons for the expedition against Persia; Antipater

topics.title: 1.3 Character, Religious Beliefs and Macedonian Warfare
points: Alexander's character and beliefs
The use of the cavalry; the use of the phalanx; the use of specialist troops; the weapons and armour of the army

sections.title: Key Topic 2: Granicus, Tyre, Egypt, Gaugamela & Persepolis (334–330 BC)

topics.title: 2.1 Battle of the Granicus and the Gordian Knot
points: The Battles at the Granicus; the events of the Battles at the Granicus; the significance of the tactics used at the main battles

topics.title: 2.2 Siege of Tyre, Issus Artefacts and Foundation Cities
points: The use of siege warfare at Tyre; the actions of Alexander and his army during the final capture of Tyre
The nature and role of his foundation cities
prescribedSetSources: Mosaic from the House of the Faun in Pompeii depicting Darius and Alexander
The Alexander sarcophagus, showing Alexander at the Battle of Issus

topics.title: 2.3 Battle of Gaugamela, Persian Gates and Burning of Persepolis
points: The Battles at Gaugamela and the Persian Gates; the events of the Battles at Gaugamela
The burning of Persepolis
prescribedSetSources: Babylonian Astronomical Diary tablet mentioning the Battle of Gaugamela

sections.title: Key Topic 3: Central Asia, Persian Customs, Conspiracies & India (330–325 BC)

topics.title: 3.1 Pursuits of Darius and Bessus, Parmenio and Murder of Cleitus
points: The pursuits of Darius and Bessus; the murder of Cleitus
His relationships with companions including Parmenio, Cleitus

topics.title: 3.2 Persian Dress, Proskynesis and Callisthenes
points: The adoption of Persian dress and customs; the changing aims of his expeditions and changing views of Persians and the Persian empire
His relationships with companions including Callisthenes

topics.title: 3.3 Aornus Rock, Indus Valley Campaign and Mutiny at the Hyphasis
points: The use of siege warfare at the Aornus Rock
The final campaign in the Indus Valley including the mutiny at the Hyphasis
prescribedSetSources: Silver tetradrachm minted by Ptolemy I showing Alexander with elephant scalp headdress

sections.title: Key Topic 4: Return to Babylon, Susa, Hephaestion & Alexander's Death (325–323 BC)

topics.title: 4.1 Return Journey, Mass Marriages at Susa and Army Relations
points: The difficulties encountered on the return journey to Babylon
The mass marriages at Susa; Alexander's relationship with his army

topics.title: 4.2 Hephaestion's Death and Royal Grief
points: The course of his life and his relationships with companions including Hephaestion

topics.title: 4.3 Alexander's Death in Babylon and Differing Explanations
points: Alexander's death and the differing explanations of the events surrounding it
